title: Life Insurance Explained: Term, Whole of Life & Trusts
description: Life insurance basics: level and decreasing term, whole of life, critical illness, income protection, writing a policy in trust and how much cover to get.
intro: Life insurance pays out if you die during the policy, so the people who depend on your income can keep their home and plans on track. Here’s how the main types work and what to think about before you buy.

blocks.title: The main types of life cover

items.title: Level term
items.text: Pays a fixed lump sum if you die within the term. Common for family protection.

items.title: Decreasing term
items.text: The payout falls over time, usually matching a repayment mortgage. Often cheaper.

items.title: Family income benefit
items.text: Pays a regular income until the end of the term rather than a lump sum.

items.title: Whole of life
items.text: Covers you for life, so it always pays out eventually. Costs much more; sometimes used for inheritance tax planning.

items.title: Critical illness
items.text: Pays a lump sum on diagnosis of listed serious illnesses. Definitions vary by insurer.

items.title: Income protection
items.text: Replaces part of your income if illness or injury stops you working, after a waiting period.

sections.html: Start with what would need paying if you died: the outstanding mortgage and other debts, plus the income your family would lose until children are independent, and costs like childcare. Subtract existing cover such as death in service from your employer. A regulated adviser can help with complex situations.

Putting a life policy in trust can mean the payout goes directly to your chosen beneficiaries without waiting for probate, and in many cases keeps it outside your estate for inheritance tax. Most insurers provide free trust forms; take advice if your situation is complicated.

US policies come as term life (for a set number of years) and permanent life (whole life and universal life, which include a cash value element). Many employers provide group life cover, often a multiple of salary, but it usually ends when you leave the job. Insurers are regulated by state insurance departments.

Answer health, smoking and lifestyle questions accurately. Misrepresentation can lead to a claim being reduced or refused, which is the worst possible outcome for a family. Life insurance is also exempt from UK Insurance Premium Tax.

faqs.q: Do I need life insurance if I’m single with no dependants?
faqs.a: Often not, unless someone else would be left with debts. Income protection may be more relevant if you rely on your own salary.

faqs.q: Is joint life cover cheaper than two single policies?
faqs.a: Often slightly cheaper, but joint policies usually pay out only once, on the first death. Two single policies pay twice.

faqs.q: Is life insurance taxed in the UK?
faqs.a: Life insurance is exempt from Insurance Premium Tax. Payouts may count towards your estate for inheritance tax unless written in trust.
